findings.text: a RACI built for the task shows whether agreed roles and practice were in place (3a) before the tree asks whether anyone knowingly departed from them (3c)
findings.problem: The repair widened the audit's fix ('agreed roles') to 'agreed roles and practice'. A RACI records who is responsible, accountable, consulted and informed; it does not show whether an accepted practice or protocol existed, which is what NHS 3a asks.
findings.evidence: Letaw deep ref L73: RACI is 'a chart for defining who is responsible (R) and accountable (A) for a task or deliverable, and who should be consulted (C) or informed (I)'. NHS deep ref L66: 3a 'Are there agreed protocols/accepted practice in place that apply to the action/omission in question?'. Audit D017 fix: 'shows whether agreed roles were in place (3a)'.
findings.fix: correct: a RACI built for the task shows whether agreed roles were in place (3a) before the tree asks whether anyone knowingly departed from them (3c)

findings.text: | Team agrees quickly on an experiment | Sequential reveal may have anchored the vote | Run fist of five; anyone at two or fewer fingers is the cue to stop, discuss and re-vote |
findings.problem: The repair (audit D012) removed 'with simultaneous reveal' from the follow-up but left the diagnosis, which still ties fist of five to a reveal-order/anchoring rationale the source does not give it (audit notes: simultaneous reveal and anti-anchoring belong to planning poker). The row is now incoherent: the follow-up no longer addresses the diagnosed cause.
findings.evidence: Deep ref L75 / source 1190-1215: fist of five = each person holds up a fist or up to five fingers; on two or fewer the team can stop, discuss, make changes and vote again; nothing on reveal order or anchoring. Simultaneous reveal is planning poker (deep ref L89).
findings.fix: correct: | Team agrees quickly on an experiment | Quick agreement can hide dissent nobody has voiced | Run fist of five; anyone at two or fewer fingers is the cue to stop, discuss and re-vote |

findings.text: | Experiment has "team responsible" as owner | RACI's Accountable cell is empty; no individual owns the outcome | Name one person as Accountable before the retro closes |
findings.problem: Unchanged line carrying the same single-named-Accountable premise the repair removed from L59 and L104 (audit D010/D018, graded UNSUPPORTED). Letaw gives no one-person rule for the A cell; her own example fills A cells with roles and puts two As on one task.
findings.evidence: Deep ref L73: Accountable = 'Who will approve the work and make sure it gets done.' Source 1082-1167: example matrix uses roles (Frontend Lead, Backend Lead, Team Lead) in A cells; 'One person might have multiple roles.'
findings.fix: correct: | Experiment has "team responsible" as owner | RACI gap: nobody knows who will approve the work and make sure it gets done, which raises the odds the experiment is dropped | Fill the Accountable cell before the retro closes |
